defects.summary: hooks/mcp-liveness/liveness.py follows a config-supplied endpoint's redirect into the loopback range and emits a SYN to 169.254.169.254. An untrusted repo that ships an MCP config chooses the destination (AGENTS.md 9). Fix: resolve the host and reject private/loopback/link-local before connecting, and disable redirect following on a liveness probe.

scholarly_access/policy.ALLOW_HOST_FRAGMENTS is matched with 'frag in host', so any attacker-registered host containing 'repository', 'dspace', 'eprints', '.edu' or '.ac.uk' passes; download_oa_pdf then never re-validates the redirect target. Fix: anchor the fragment match to a label boundary, re-run assert_lawful on every hop, and block private ranges after DNS resolution.

omniaudit sitelint crawls a caller-supplied URL with httpx follow_redirects=True and then screenshots the redirected page with headless Chromium, writing an internal response into a durable PNG. Fix: a private-range block before both the httpx fetch and the browser navigation.
download_oa_pdf returns the first 5 bytes plus the status of the fetched internal response to its caller, converting a blind SSRF into a small read oracle.

Repo-wide: 0 of 106 files with a fetch call site perform any private/link-local range check. The defense exists nowhere, so every future fetch stage starts undefended. Fix: one shared guarded client (http_secure.py is the working model) that every stage is required to use.

report.question: Which stages can be induced to issue a request to an attacker-chosen host or a link-local/internal address, and is there an allowlist, a redirect cap and a private-range block?
report.answer: Four of the five stages driven live can be induced; the fifth cannot. Repo-wide there is NO private-range block anywhere (0 of 106 files), an allowlist in only 3 files, and every redirect cap in the tree except two is the library default rather than a program control. The single strongest vector is the pair 'allowlist checked once on the entry URL' + 'client follows redirects by default': it converts a one-time host check into no check at all.
